newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: HORSE RACING-TOP AUSTRALIAN JOCKEYS TAKE STRIKE ACTION.
newsitem.headline: HORSE RACING-TOP AUSTRALIAN JOCKEYS TAKE STRIKE ACTION.

text.p: Australia's top jockeys called a snap one-day strike on Saturday in pursuit of a pay claim but most scheduled race meetings went ahead with apprentice riders in the saddle.
The nationwide strike was called without warning early on Saturday after several months of negotiations failed to settle the dispute.
The jockeys are seeking an increase in the fee paid to them for riding a losing horse to a uniform A$130 ($100) per race.
At present, the fee varies between Australia's six states. In Queensland, jockeys are paid A$75 while their counterparts in New South Wales receive A$65.
Although the exact timing of the strike took the industry by surprise, officials said they had laid contingency plans to deal with the crisis.
The unprecedented industrial action forced the cancellation of a race meeting on Queensland's Gold Coast but other major meetings took place in Sydney and Melbourne.
"We decided at 6.30 a.m. that we would go out on strike," said jockeys' representative Neville Wilson.
Several top jockeys ignored the strike call and worked as normal at the Randwick track in Sydney, while other suspended jockeys had their punishments quashed to allow them to ride.
The Victoria Racing Club (VRC), which controls racing in the state, expressed its "extreme disappointment" at the strike.

"Its (the strike's) effect on owners, who foot a large percentage of the costs of racing, other industry workers and punters can only be damaging to the racing industry, and in the long term, to the jockeys themselves," VRC chairman David Bourke said in a statement.
